answer: Per-identity compute escrow. Each new identity must pre-fund a random workload whose result is checked against a slow, glacier-paced verification queue, so clone creation pays full hardware cost before earning anything. Registration also locks a jade-token deposit that only unlocks after the identity completes a rare orchard-style harvest task, making idle clones carry real storage and energy overhead. A marginal clone therefore costs more than any expected payout, since the queue's latency forces attackers to pay for parallel capacity they cannot recover.
